headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress make Cline dangerous with Airbyte outputs; prompt-injection and cascading-error risks are also material.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airbyte can emit data via its API and broad network egress, while Cline reads workspace files and uses MCP/browser tools. If Airbyte outputs are copied into files or prompts, Cline can treat attacker-controlled content as instructions. The shared-file bridge is plausible, though not proven by docs alone.
conditions: IF Airbyte output is written into a workspace file that Cline reads
IF Cline ingests that file content as instructions or tool arguments
mitigations: Keep Airbyte outputs in a separate, read-only folder
Add a manual review step before Cline reads any Airbyte-generated file
Disable MCP servers that can execute instructions from file content
Use a prompt firewall or delimiter wrapper for imported text

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress; Cline reads and writes workspace files, handles model-provider API keys, and can use browsers and MCP. In a shared workspace, sensitive Airbyte data can flow into Cline’s context and then out through its configured model provider or browser actions. This is a default-dangerous pairwise leakage path.
conditions: IF Airbyte processes business data in the same workspace or adjacent files Cline can read
IF Cline sends workspace contents to its model provider or browser targets
mitigations: Isolate Airbyte outputs in a separate workspace
Redact sensitive fields before Cline opens any files
Restrict Cline to local-only tasks when handling business data
Rotate any exposed model-provider keys immediately
Use per-project credentials and least-privilege access

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte can call APIs and egress broadly, while Cline can write files, modify git state, execute shells, and run browsers. Cline’s workspace-scoped shared state plus Airbyte’s external data movement creates overlapping mutable surfaces without documented locking between the pair, so concurrent edits or pipeline changes can collide and corrupt state.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace
IF Airbyte-generated artifacts are committed or rewritten while Cline is editing them
mitigations: Assign separate workspaces for Airbyte and Cline
Pause one agent before the other mutates shared files
Use git branches with manual merge review
Enable file-locking or a single-writer policy
Keep generated artifacts out of version control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airbyte can produce transformed data or pipeline outputs, and Cline can act on files, git state, and browser sessions. If Cline treats Airbyte outputs as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into code changes or external actions. The pair is risky by default, but the blast radius is usually bounded by reviewable work products.
conditions: IF Cline uses Airbyte-produced artifacts as ground truth
IF Cline commits or acts on those artifacts without independent validation
mitigations: Require a human review of Airbyte outputs before Cline uses them
Add schema and checksum validation on imported artifacts
Limit Cline to drafting changes, not applying them automatically
Keep downstream actions behind explicit approval gates

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and Cline handles workspace files plus model-provider API keys, so compliance depends on where data is stored and which provider receives it. The profiles do not show a residency mismatch or regulated data class like PHI, so this is a policy-mismatch risk rather than a breach certainty. I cite both because the flow spans both agents.
conditions: IF business data is routed through a model provider with a different retention policy
IF workspace files containing regulated data are retained beyond policy
mitigations: Document retention and deletion rules for both tools
Avoid placing regulated data in Cline-readable workspaces
Use a provider with an approved DPA and residency setting
Purge temporary files after each session
